timeline.title: A Short History of Anniversaries
items: Middle Ages
Silver and gold
In parts of medieval Germany, the story goes, wives wore a silver wreath at 25 years and gold at 50.
A diamond year
Queen Victoria marked sixty years on the throne with a Diamond Jubilee. Diamond has meant sixty ever since.
Paper, wood and tin
Emily Post's famous etiquette book listed a gift for the big anniversaries, from paper in year one to gold.
A gift for every year
Jewellers in America grew the list so that almost every year had its own present, from paper to diamond.
today: Year {years} of the greatest love story never told. Until now.

letters.title: What the Poets Say About Lasting Love
items: Grow old along with me! The best is yet to be.
Robert Browning, Rabbi Ben Ezra, 1864
I love you without knowing how, or when, or from where.
Pablo Neruda, One Hundred Love Sonnets
Two souls with but a single thought, two hearts that beat as one.
Friedrich Halm, Ingomar the Barbarian
The heart that loves is always young.
An old saying
letters.hand: The poets say it beautifully. We just say: here is to many more years of {who}.

facts.title: The Science of Lasting Love
items: spark
Still that spark
Some couples together for decades still show the brain activity of new love at each other's photo.
smile
Laugh together
Couples who laugh together tend to feel closer, and happier in their relationship.
heart
Five to one
Happy couples share about five kind moments for every grumpy one, even in the middle of a row.
leaf
Like swans
Swans often stay with the same partner for many years, raising their young together.
sun
Good morning, dear
Some seahorse couples greet each other every morning with a little dance, brightening as they go.
hands
Thank you matters
Feeling appreciated by a partner is linked to happier, longer lasting love.
facts.hand: Science can explain a lot. It still cannot explain how {who} make it look so easy.

note.title: What we believe lasting love is
paras: We make magazines for a living, but some feel different. This was one of them.
We believe love that lasts is built from small things: the tea brought without asking, the joke that still works years later, the hand that finds yours in the dark.
{who}, one of you came to us wanting something special. Not a card anyone could buy, but pages full of your story: your faces, your jokes, the moments only you two share.
And from everything we were told, this love is only getting better with time.
note.wish: Happy anniversary, {who}. Here is to forever, and a little longer.
